design_rule: The finale strengthens—not suppresses—the countercase. It returns to the original elevator only for the explicit spoken callback, and it ends on an inspection method rather than an asset recommendation.

clusters.purpose: Put the concentrated-basket, defensive-asset, long-tail, and memory-cycle counterarguments on screen before returning to the thesis.
clusters.asset_strategy: use the countercase plate only for the memory-specific risks; use deterministic source cards or neutral reframes for equal-weight and index-healing claims; never use the plate as evidence for those separate mechanisms.
must_not_imply: the long tail is dead weight

clusters.purpose: Restate the bounded thesis: broad indexing solves low-cost participation; a two-sleeve framework is a testable design hypothesis, not a model portfolio; both trades can bubble.
clusters.asset_strategy: use purpose-matched returns to the memory capacity, index container, and barbell worlds only as each underlying mechanism is named; no decorative montage or unsupported asset reuse.
must_not_imply: sell the index and buy memory
one trade is certainly a bubble

clusters.purpose: Close on the reusable inspection method: look under the elevator, identify who pays, what is scarce, how supply responds, and whether cash flow or resale belief sustains demand.
clusters.asset_strategy: return to wrong-bubble-elevators-v2 only on the explicit elevator callback, with the caption/evidence field used for the four inspection questions; final frame holds the two separate upside-and-defense jobs.
